# Mapping a whole diocese

You own the diocese until its PR is open. The rules are in `explore-diocese` and
`data/dioceses/README.md`; read both before you start. This page covers how to split the
work so it uses as little of the usage limit as it can.

## Why the work is split this way

An agent reads its whole context again on every step, so the cost of running one grows
with the square of how long it runs. Scranton, Allentown and Harrisburg each ran as six or
seven region agents of 10 to 17 parishes, all at once and all on Opus. Each cost $60 to $100,
about two-thirds of it spent re-reading contexts that had grown past 400k tokens of bulletin
text, probe output and screenshots. In Allentown, four of the six agents hit the usage
limit, and each resume rebuilt a large context.

So:

- **Bulky reading happens in short-lived contexts.** A `parish-scout` agent
  (`.claude/agents/parish-scout.md`, on Sonnet) researches about four parishes, writes their
  records and ends. The records, with their quoted evidence, are the result, so its report
  to you is a few lines.
- **Your context stays small.** Don't read bulletins, PDFs, probe output, rosters or whole
  records yourself. Work from command summaries (`todo`, `coverage`, `audit`, `validate`,
  `search`) and scout reports, filtered with `jq`. Read a record only to settle a question
  that spans batches.
- **One scout at a time.** Each scout starts from what the earlier ones learned, and the
  run never stalls at the usage limit with several half-finished agents. Run two at once
  only if the user asks for speed.
- **What scouts learn goes into files, not into your context.** The playbook is the
  diocese's `diocese.md`; reusable scripts go in the tools folder. After the diocese, lessons
  that apply everywhere go into the README, a skill or the CLI, where the next diocese gets
  them for free.

## 1. Set up

1. `pnpm diocese init <d> ...` and `pnpm diocese roster fetch <d> gcatholic`. If the
   diocese's directory runs WP Store Locator, `roster fetch <d> wpsl <URL>`. If scraping it
   takes more than reading one page, give it to a scout as a task (section 4).
2. Run `.claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh` once, so scouts don't
   each install Chrome.
3. Make the scratch folders (`scratch/` is ignored by git):
   `mkdir -p scratch/map-<d>/tools scratch/map-<d>/scouts` and start
   `scratch/map-<d>/tools/README.md` with one line saying what the folder is for.
4. Read the structure: the diocese's family or cluster list, its closed-parishes page, its
   pastoral plan. Write what you find in `diocese.md` *Sources*. This is the one place you
   read source pages yourself, because the batches depend on it.
5. Copy the playbook from the dioceses already mapped: in `diocese.md`, fill in the
   *Bulletin publishers here* section that `init` put under *Sources* with what earlier
   dioceses in the same reg

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span

   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.

```
## `render.py`: read a bulletin page that is only an image

Many bulletins are scanned images, in whole or in part: in Syracuse, about one in five
(ParishesOnline, Discover Mass and self-hosted alike). `probe pdf` lists those pages under
`pages_without_text`. The sandbox has no pdftoppm, PIL or tesseract, so `render.py` draws
the pages with pdf.js in Chrome and writes PNGs you can look at with the Read tool:

```bash
uv run python .claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/render.py \
    https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/03/1424/20260920B.pdf /tmp/ccsssp --pages 1-2
```

`--pages` takes numbers and ranges (`1,3-5`); without it every page is drawn.

Cite the PDF's URL as usual, and say in the evidence `note` that the page is an image, so
the auditor knows `recheck` can't find the quote in its text. Record in the parish's
*Website and bulletin provider* that the bulletin is image-only: the pipeline will need to
read it as an image too.

## `finder.py`: an eCatholic parish finder as a roster

   family or cluster site. It may be blocked too, but it's worth one try.
3. **Try `visit.py` again later.** Blocked streaks pass.

## `issues.py`: probe container for eCatholic and Discover Mass

`probe container` walks a ParishesOnline container back week by week, and `issues.py` does
the same for the other two publishers. Their files live on hosts with no Cloudflare, so no
browser is needed even when the parish's own site is blocked:

```bash
I=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/issues.py"
uv run python $I ecatholic ecatholic:20434 [--weeks 12 --from 2026-06-01 --step 4 --all --pages 3 --grep "St. Anne"]
uv run python $I discovermass discovermass:st-patrick-victor-ny [--issues 6 --pages 3]
```

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote
<d> --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote <d>` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline
command seeds the new rows into the data

---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.
… [3334 chars truncated]
```

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote
<d> --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote <d>` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline
command seeds the new rows into the data
… [6828 chars truncated]

---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.
… [3351 chars truncated]
```

## `issues.py`: probe container for eCatholic and Discover Mass

`probe container` walks a ParishesOnline container back week by week, and `issues.py` does
the same for the other two publishers. Their files live on hosts with no Cloudflare, so no
browser is needed even when the parish's own site is blocked:

```bash
I=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/issues.py"
uv run python $I ecatholic ecatholic:20434 [--weeks 12 --from 2026-06-01 --step 4 --all --pages 3 --grep "St. Anne"]
uv run python $I discovermass discovermass:st-patrick-victor-ny [--issues 6 --pages 3]
```

- **eCatholic:** issues are at `files.ecatholic.com/{site id}/bulletins/{YYYYMMDD}.pdf`, one
  per Sunday. The coming Sunday's issue is usually up by mid-week. As with ParishesOnline,
  **a missing issue answers 403, not 404**, and there's no directory listing. The site id
  comes from `visit.py` on the parish's eCatholic site. Without `--from`, it starts at the
  coming Sunday. With `--from`, it starts at the Sunday on or before that date, as
  `probe container --from` does. Some parishes date the file by another weekday: Holy
  Spirit, Hamilton posts the 27 September issue as `20260925.pdf`, the Friday before. Pass
  `--day fri` (or `sat`, ...) for those.
- **`ecatholic:31250` is the Diocese of Syracuse's own site**, not a parish. `visit.py` and
  `probe url` report it on any parish page that links a diocesan PDF. Don't record it.
- **Discover Mass:** the church page is server-rendered and lists about

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote
<d> --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote <d>` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline
command seeds the new rows into the data

```
---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.
… [2338 chars truncated]
```

import sys,re
# usage: fill.py record.md evidence.yaml body.md [set key=value ...]
p,ev,body=sys.argv[1:4]
sets=dict(a.split('=',1) for a in sys.argv[4:])
t=open(p).read()
m=re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---\n',t,re.S)
fm=m.group(1)
evt=open(ev).read().rstrip('\n')
if re.search(r'^evidence: \[\]$',fm,re.M):
    fm=re.sub(r'^evidence: \[\]$','evidence:\n'+evt,fm,flags=re.M)
else:
    fm=fm+'\n'+evt
for k,v in sets.items():
    if re.search(rf'^{k}:.*$',fm,re.M): fm=re.sub(rf'^{k}:.*$',f'{k}: {v}',fm,flags=re.M)
    else: fm+=f'\n{k}: {v}'
open(p,'w').write('---\n'+fm+'\n---\n\n'+open(body).read().strip('\n')+'\n')
```

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote

---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.
… [3390 chars truncated]

Catholic Campus Ministries
The Mission of Catholic Campus Ministry at Juniata College is to be a sign and witness of the presence of Christ at Juniata College. We strive to be a guide in relation to the Catholic perspective while creating a welcoming, diverse, and supportive campus community. Through our Catholic Tradition, we give students the background and the confidence necessary to share and live the gospel in their life journey. Catholic Campus Ministry is a commissioned office of the Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown.
In addition to offering Mass on campus at 6 pm Sundays in the Global Commons of Tussey Hall, Catholic Campus Ministry also has weekly meetings of Catholic Council (a student organization) and offers Confession Saturdays at 3:00 at Most Holy Trinity Church or available upon request on campus. There is also a broad resource library available at the Unity House.
Opportunities are available to be involved as a Liturgical Minister - If you have the desire or feel the call to serve and share your gift to read, sing, or play the keyboard, we would love to have you join our team. Contact Lisa, Catholic Campus Minister, at baerl@juniata.edu to learn more.

About St. Catherine of Siena Catholic Church

     St. Catherine of Siena Catholic Church was established in 1912, when Bishop Eugene Garvey of the Altoona Diocese gave permission for the building of a Church in Mount Union. It began as a mission of Most Holy Trinity Church in Huntingdon, PA, and became an independent parish on July 1, 1921. St. Mary Parish in Shade Gap became a Mission of St. Catherine until becoming an independent parish in June 7, 1962.

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

- `discovermass-church-urls.txt`: all 20,279 Discover Mass church page URLs (from `wp-sitemap-posts-item-1..11.xml` on discovermass.com, 2026-10-21); `grep -i <town>` finds a church's slug when `?s=` search is broken. A page's "Visit Website" link gives the parish's homepage.
- `fill_record.py <record.md> <evidence.yaml> <body.md> [key=value ...]`: replaces a freshly created record's `evidence: []` (or appends to its evidence list) with the YAML items in a file, replaces the body with a Markdown file, and sets frontmatter keys. Run with `python3 -I`. Quote any `quote:` value containing ": " yourself.

## assistant — 2026-10-21T17:58:56.931407Z

Batch 6 of 24 is committed and pushed, along with a bug fix it turned up. Batch 7 (Bedford and Fulton counties) is now running.

- **Bug fix:** the bulletin downloader crashed when a file name contained a dash character like "–", as Huntingdon's does. I fixed it in `src/pdf_extract/fetch.py` and added a test. That test fails without the fix and the fetch tests pass with it. Huntingdon's bulletin now downloads.
- **Rows:** Huntingdon and Mount Union each publish their own bulletin. Dudley and Shade Gap post none, so they're marked "no bulletin", stay off the site, and get a recheck at the end of December. Both parish pairs share clergy but not a bulletin, so they stay as separate rows.
- **Juniata College:** the directory lists a Sunday Mass at the college, but no source says it's open to the public, so it's held as an open question.

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote

  Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all:
  for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that
  doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis.
- **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s.
- **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15,

href="gallery/STATEMENT REGARDING CHURCH GROUNDS.pdf"

`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:

1. **Locate** the bulletin page by following the homepage's "bulletin" links
   (`locate.py`).
2. **Collect** the PDFs it offers (`collectors.py`). Each collector handles one
   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link
   is the PDF), `page-pdfs` (links, or addresses in the page's markup),
   `linked-issue-page` (an embedded flipbook or a publisher's listing) and
   `dated-post` (a weekly post that wraps the PDF). They run in that order
   until one finds a convincing set. `page-pdfs` also reads PDF addresses a
   viewer plugin keeps in base64 JSON (PDF Embedder's `pdfemb-data`, 3D
   FlipBook's `FB3D_CLIENT_DATA`), and takes Google Drive files, Google Docs
   (exported as PDF), Concrete CMS and DotNetNuke (`LinkClick.aspx`) downloads
   as PDFs. One more collector runs only when a recipe names it:
   `page-images`, for a parish that posts each issue as an image (a JPEG per
   weekend); `fetch` stores the image as a one-page PDF.
3. **Choose** this week's issue among them (`choose.py`), and say why:
   `current` (dated this week), or a fallback (`newest-recent`, `titled`,
   `first-listed`). `newest-recent` is the newest issue dated in the last 45
   days, taken when the first listed is plainly old, or when it is neither
   dated nor labelled "bulletin" and the page lists a dated series.

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote

command seeds the new rows into the data

Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher,

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote

#### How the `other` resolver reads a site

`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:

1. **Locate** the bulletin page by following the homepage's "bulletin" links
   (`locate.py`).
2. **Collect** the PDFs it offers (`collectors.py`). Each collector handles one
   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link
   is the PDF), `page-pdfs` (links, or addresses in the page's markup),
   `linked-issue-page` (an embedded flipbook or a publisher's listing) and
   `dated-post` (a weekly post that wraps the PDF). They run in that order
   until one finds a convincing set. `page-pdfs` also reads PDF addresses a
   viewer plugin keeps in base64 JSON (PDF Embedder's `pdfemb-data`, 3D
   FlipBook's `FB3D_CLIENT_DATA`), and takes Google Drive files, Google Docs
   (exported as PDF), Concrete CMS and DotNetNuke (`LinkClick.aspx`) downloads
   as PDFs. One more collector runs only when a recipe names it:
   `page-images`, for a parish that posts each issue as an image (a JPEG per
   weekend); `fetch` stores the image as a one-page PDF.

The fix is small: read an 8-digit `MMDDYYYY` run as a date, but only when its year is within one year of today, so 8-digit ids elsewhere don't turn into dates. Adding it with tests.

**tool_use** `Bash`
```

 "command": "python3 - <<'EOF'\np='src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/dates.py'\ns=open(p).read()\nold='''    # Slugs and file names join words with hyphens or underscores'''\nnew='''    # Or as MMDDYYYY (\"10112026.jpg\", St. Anne, Davidsville's Wix image). Only a\n    # year next to the reference date's, so an eight-digit id doesn't read as one.\n    for match in re.finditer(r\"(?<!\\\\d)(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(0[1-9]|[12]\\\\d|3[01])(20\\\\d{2})(?!\\\\d)\", normalized):\n        month, day, match_year = (int(part) for part in match.groups())\n        if abs(match_year - reference_date.year) <= 1:\n            parsed = safe_date(match_year, month, day)\n            if parsed is not None:\n                return parsed\n\n    # Slugs and file names join words with hyphens or underscores'''\nassert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1); open(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ngrep -ln \"parse_date\" tests/*.py | head",
 "description": "Add MMDDYYYY date form with year guard"
}

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

Exit code 5
7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.
… [3351 chars truncated]

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

"""`probe url` with a real browser: see a parish website the way a person does.

`pnpm diocese probe url` fetches pages without a browser, so it reports
HTTP4XX for sites behind Cloudflare (every eCatholic site, many others),
NO-PARISH-WORDS for sites built in JavaScript (Wix, Squarespace, "Redirecting..."
shells), and no publications for bulletins that sit in an iframe widget or one
click deep. This opens the page in the pipeline's own stealth browser
(pdf_extract.browser.launch_stealth_browser) with real Chrome, headed under
xvfb, and reports the same fields `probe url` does, read from the rendered page
and its iframes. Run scripts/setup_browser.sh once per sandbox first.

Cloudflare decides per request whether to challenge, and in a Claude Code sandbox
the challenge can never be solved (brunhild.challenges.cloudflare.com is denied
by the egress policy), so a challenged load is simply retried with backoff.

Usage (from the repo root; re-runs itself under xvfb-run when there is no display):
  uv run python .claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py URL [URL ...] [options]

  --bulletin        when a page embeds no publication id, open its bulletin links
                    (up to 5) until one does, the way detect.py does; bulletin PDFs
                    with no publisher are reported as self-hosted (url:<page>)

                    TEXT (case-insensitive); repeat to walk deeper (sin

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.
- A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo

  bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row).
- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single
  bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate.

Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is

---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widget
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.

## Setup, once per sandbox (~1 min)

```bash
.claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh
```

This installs Google Chrome and trusts the agent proxy's TLS certificate in Chrome's store.

"""`probe container` for the other two bulletin publishers: eCatholic and Discover Mass.

`pnpm diocese probe container` walks a ParishesOnline container back Sunday by
Sunday; nothing in the CLI does the same for eCatholic or Discover Mass. Both
serve their bulletins from hosts that are NOT behind Cloudflare, so this needs
no browser even when the parish's own eCatholic site is challenged:

  ecatholic     files.ecatholic.com/{site id}/bulletins/{YYYYMMDD}.pdf, one per Sunday.
                Like ParishesOnline, a missing issue answers 403 (S3 AccessDenied),
                not 404, and there is no directory listing.
  discovermass  discovermass.com/church/{slug}/ is server-rendered and lists the
                current issue plus an archive of about 12, each a download.php link.

Takes the publication id as `probe url`/visit.py report it (ecatholic:20434,
discovermass:st-patrick-victor-ny), the bare id/slug, or any URL containing it.

Usage (from the repo root):
  uv run python .claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/issues.py ecatholic <id> \
      [--weeks 12] [--from DATE] [--step N] [--all] [--day fri] [--pages N] [--grep TEXT ...]
  uv run python .claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/issues.py discovermass <slug> \
      [--issues 6] [--pages N] [--grep TEXT ...]

--pages N adds the text of the first N readable pages of each issue found (the
masthead is often on page 2 or 3), and --grep counts and quotes a term per page,
exactly as `probe pdf` does (--grep alone
… [739 chars truncated]
```

def _download_bulletin(
    *, fetch_url: str, source_url: str, validators: Validators | None = None,
) -> Download:
    """Download a bulletin, asking first whether `validators` still name it."""
    conditional = validators.request_headers() if validators else {}

    def get() -> _Response:
        return _http_get(fetch_url, referer=source_url, extra_headers=conditional)

    try:
        LOGGER.info("Attempting primary fetch URL: %s", fetch_url)
        try:
            response = get()
        except HTTPError as exc:
            # Weebly and Wix file hosts answer 429 to a few quick requests.
            if exc.code != HTTPStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS:
                raise
            LOGGER.warning("429 from %s; retrying in %ss", fetch_url, HTTP_429_RETRY_SECONDS)
            time.sleep(HTTP_429_RETRY_SECONDS)
            response = get()

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not

- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single

Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.

Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST

  Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and
  Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the
  roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and
  (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins.

### Checking the fetch stage

Most parishes publish through ParishesOnline, eCatholic or Discover Mass, but
the `other` provider has to find the bulletin on the parish's own website, and
every site is laid out differently. `pnpm fetch:check` runs the resolvers in the
browser without touching the database, downloads what each one picks, and
prints one row per parish (`ok`, `resolve_failed`, `download_failed`,
`not_pdf`, or `blocked` when Cloudflare challenged the browser instead).

#### How the `other` resolver reads a site

`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:

1. **Locate** the bulletin page by following the homepage's "bulletin" links
   (`locate.py`).
2. **Collect** the PDFs it offers (`collectors.py`). Each collector handles one
   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link
   is the PDF), `page-pdfs` (links, or addresses in the page's markup),
   `linked-issue-page` (an embedded flipbook or a publisher's listing) and
   `dated-post` (a weekly post that wraps the PDF). They run in that order
   until one finds a convincing set. `page-pdfs` also reads PDF addresses a
   viewer plugin keeps in base64 JSON (PDF Embedder's `pdfemb-data`, 3D
   Flip

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [Files](#files): layout and fields

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one

- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single

Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.

## assistant — 2026-10-21T19:27:41.411438Z

Batch 14 of 24 is committed and pushed, with no validation errors. Batch 15 is running now: St. Francis and St. Clement in Johnstown, and Transfiguration and St. John Vianney, which share a website.

What batch 14 found:
- **St. Anne and St. Therese** share one website but publish two separate bulletins, so they are two rows. Both downloaded in the check. The weak spot: the fetcher picks a file by its date and place in the list, not its name. Each row therefore relies on its own bulletin being listed first on a different page of the site. If the parish reorders its pages, one row could pick up the other parish's bulletin. I've written this risk into both records and will list a file-name filter as a suggested improvement in the PR.
- **Visitation** has a bulletin site that only turned up through a web search. The fetcher reads it through the site's news feed, because the page itself hides the PDF links.
- **Sts. Gregory and Barnabas** has no bulletin anywhere the scout could find, so it is marked "no bulletin" for now. Batch 15 is checking whether a neighbour's bulletin carries it.

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),

church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

485-
486-`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:

491-   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link

497-   FlipBook's `FB3D_CLIENT_DATA`), and takes Google Drive files, Google Docs

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheap

are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.
- A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo
  had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while
  St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish

  after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7
  bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row).
- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single
  bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate.

Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.

**One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories,

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to

church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheap

---
name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0
---

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST
  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,

is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader
needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet

done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't.

record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it.

- **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites*

  provider*, *Not yet confirmed*.
- **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement,
  coordinates).
- **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change
  this*.
- **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*.

Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote`
refuses until none are left.

## `visit.py`: probe url in a real browser

```bash
V=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py"
uv run python $V --bulletin https://www.stmarys-clinton.com http://saintlouisgonzaga.org   # like probe url
uv run python $V https://stleohilton.org --follow /bulletins --links --match files.ecatholic
uv run python $V https://example-parish.org --text --chars 3000 --screenshot /tmp/p.png   # Read the PNG
```

It prints JSON with `probe url`'s fields for the site's own page, judged on the **rendered**
HTML of the page and its iframes:

- **`verdict`:** `probe url`'s checks (SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX,
  NO-PARISH-WORDS, ok) applied to the rendered HTML, plus two of its own. `BLOCKED` means
  Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all:
  for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that
  doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis.
- **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s.
- **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15,
  and WordPress pages use those up on feeds before reaching the PDF.
- **`--bulletin`:** when the page embeds no id, it opens the site's bulletin pages (up to 5)
  until one does. The result goes in `bulletin_search.found`. Bulletin PDFs with no
  publisher are reported as self-hosted, with `url:<the page that lists them>`. That

import sys,re
# usage: fill.py record.md evidence.yaml body.md [set key=value ...]
p,ev,body=sys.argv[1:4]
sets=dict(a.split('=',1) for a in sys.argv[4:])
t=open(p).read()
m=re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---\n',t,re.S)
fm=m.group(1)
evt=open(ev).read().rstrip('\n')
if re.search(r'^evidence: \[\]$',fm,re.M):
    fm=re.sub(r'^evidence: \[\]$','evidence:\n'+evt,fm,flags=re.M)
else:
    fm=fm+'\n'+evt
for k,v in sets.items():
    if re.search(rf'^{k}:.*$',fm,re.M): fm=re.sub(rf'^{k}:.*$',f'{k}: {v}',fm,flags=re.M)
    else: fm+=f'\n{k}: {v}'
open(p,'w').write('---\n'+fm+'\n---\n\n'+open(body).read().strip('\n')+'\n')

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

---
name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of

  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,
